nodes.label: What signs do and shape-color meanings

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F01 explains that fixed shape-and-color meanings let drivers read a sign at once and that any rectangle regulates, while sec04-R02 lists the color code itself; learners think shape alone carries no meaning

nodes.label: Stop, all-way, yield and prohibition signs

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F02 describes the four sign types including the all-way plate and the slashed red ring, while sec04-R01 contrasts only stop with yield; learners treat a yield as a full stop

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F03 gives the complete color list with fluorescent yellow-green for schools, pedestrians, and bicyclists, while sec04-R02 compresses it; learners confuse orange construction warning with yellow general warning

nodes.label: Harming signs is a crime

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

nodes.no_confusable_reason: the sign-tampering statute has no sibling rule in this section that learners swap it with

nodes.label: Regulatory signs, school zones and disabled spaces

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F05 covers the general regulatory sign plus school-zone slowing and disabled spaces, while sec04-F06 lists lane-use and turn-ban panels; learners think regulatory signs are advice rather than law

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F06 lists every lane-use and ban panel, while sec04-R03 isolates the must-panel versus optional-panel contrast; learners read an optional panel as a must

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F07 lists the warning sign hazards including merges and added lanes, while sec04-R05 contrasts a merge with an added lane; learners treat an added lane as a merge

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F08 covers reflectors, stripe direction, and T-intersections, while sec04-R06 isolates the stripe direction rule; learners read the stripe direction backwards

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F09 is the full rail rule including which vehicles must stop and the no-passing rule, while sec04-R07 contrasts the round advance sign with the crossbuck; learners forget the fifteen-to-fifty-foot halt line

nodes.label: Flashing lights, gates and quiet zones

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F10 covers flashing lights, gates, and quiet zones, while sec04-R08 contrasts the light-only crossing with the gated crossing; learners move as soon as the train passes a gated crossing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F11 covers the orange devices and doubled fines, while sec04-F12 covers flagpersons and the misdemeanor penalty; learners think fines double only when a flagperson is present

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F12 adds the misdemeanor fine and jail term to the flagperson rule, while sec04-R09 keeps only the in-lane halt and obedience; learners swerve around a flagperson halt

nodes.label: Channeling devices and slow-vehicle emblem

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

nodes.no_confusable_reason: the slow-moving-vehicle emblem has no sibling rule in this section that learners swap it with

nodes.label: Guide signs, mileposts and litter

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

nodes.no_confusable_reason: guide signs and mileposts have no sibling rule in this section that learners swap them with

nodes.label: Signal colors and turns on red

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F15 is the full signal rule with green arrows and turning lanes, while sec04-R10 isolates the steady-red and flashing-red turn rules; learners think any left turn on red is allowed

nodes.label: Flashing arrows, flashing lights and signal position

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F16 covers flashing arrows and lights plus the position rule, while sec04-F15 covers steady signals and green arrows; learners confuse a flashing yellow arrow with a protected green arrow

nodes.label: Pedestrian signals, lane-control signals and stripes

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-F17 covers pedestrian signals, lane-control signals, and all stripe meanings, while sec04-R11 isolates the yellow-line passing rules; learners cross a double solid line to pass

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R01 isolates the stop-versus-yield contrast, while sec04-F02 adds the all-way plate and the prohibition ring; learners think yield means stop whenever traffic is present

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R02 compresses the color code with rectangles always regulating, while sec04-F03 lists every color including fluorescent yellow-green for schools; learners forget the yellow-green category

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R03 is the must-versus-optional contrast, while sec04-F06 gives the concrete left, straight, and right examples; learners assume every arrow panel binds the lane to one move

nodes.label: Center lane for left turns only

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R04 isolates the center-lane rule, while sec04-F06 lists it among many regulatory panels; learners use the center lane to pass

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R05 says merges fold traffic into one line while added-lane joins need no merge, and sec04-F07 lists both among the warning signs; learners slow for an added lane as if merging

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R06 is the stripe direction rule alone, while sec04-F08 adds reflectors and T-intersections; learners confuse downward-right with a left turn

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R07 splits the advance sign from the crossbuck, while sec04-F09 adds the vehicles that must stop by law; learners think the crossbuck itself orders a stop for every vehicle

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R08 says light-only crossings release when the train passes with all tracks clear while gated crossings hold until gates rise and lights die, and sec04-F10 adds quiet zones; learners think a rising gate alone frees them

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R09 is the in-lane halt rule, while sec04-F12 adds the penalty and the warning to watch for opposing traffic; learners edge forward before being waved on

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R10 contrasts steady red with flashing red and flashing red arrows, while sec04-F15 gives the full green, yellow, and red rule; learners treat a flashing red arrow like a steady red

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R11 states the yellow-line passing rules, while sec04-F17 adds that white and yellow stripes also assign lanes and mark turn spots; learners think a double solid line also bans a left-turn center crossing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: sec04-R12 isolates the three pedestrian figures, while sec04-F17 adds lane-control signals and stripes; learners start crossing on a flashing figure

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach why shape and color let a sign be read at once, then the full color code, then the law against harming signs
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on shape meaning, each sign color and the tampering statute
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on what rectangles do, which color means what and the tampering penalty

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach stop, all-way, yield and the prohibition ring, then black-and-white regulatory signs, then lane-use panels and the center lane
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on stop versus yield, school zones, disabled spaces, lane panels and the center lane
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on what each regulatory sign orders and how must-panels differ from optional panels

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach the yellow diamond warning family, then merge versus added lane, then reflectors, stripe direction and T-intersections
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on warning hazards, merges, reflectors and stripe direction
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on what diamonds announce, added lanes, stripe direction and T-intersections

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach the advance sign and crossbuck, then which vehicles must stop, then flashing lights, gates and quiet zones
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on the halt line, buses that must stop, lights, gates and quiet zones
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on the fifteen-to-fifty-foot line, what the crossbuck triggers and when gates release

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach orange work-zone devices and doubled fines, then flagpersons and the penalty, then channeling devices and the slow-vehicle emblem
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on work-zone duties, doubled fines, flagperson halts and the emblem
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on when fines double, how to respond to a flagperson and the emblem speed

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach guide signs and mileposts, then steady signals and turns on red, then flashing arrows, flashing lights and reading by position
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on guide colors, mileposts, each signal color, turns on red and flashing signals
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on milepost counting, left turns on red, flashing red arrows and signal position

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach pedestrian and lane-control signals first, then the three pedestrian figures, then the yellow-line passing rules
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact visible-answer cards on pedestrian figures, lane-control lights and yellow lines
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which signal governs a crossing, what a flashing figure means and what each yellow line allows

learning_path_rule.rule: topological prerequisite order; module order and handbook order break ties; dynamic nodes never on the path

edge_types.definition: learn the from-fact before the to-fact
pair of facts learners commonly swap

sequencing.rule: topological prerequisite order, then module order and handbook order; dynamic excluded
